title: Reliable Apply/Undo API for Optimize Recommendations with Exactly-Once Semantics
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Optimize issues recommendations (batching/caching/quantization) need a programmatic apply flow for customers and internal automation agents that is safe to retry and supports easy rollback. Current apply endpoints are best-effort and can produce duplicate or partial application when retries or controller restarts occur. We need an API and SDK primitives that provide exactly-once or at least strongly-consistent apply/undo semantics for recommendation commits and a webhook model for long-running apply/rollback operations.

Goal: Design and implement a lightweight transactional Apply API plus an accompanying Undo endpoint, a webhook lifecycle for asynchronous execution, idempotency primitives for SDKs, and operational hooks (DLQ, tracing, audit events) so Optimize automation can run reliably across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket covers API surface, server-side contract, storage design for operation log, and the SDK helper primitives for safe retries.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/optimize/apply - accepts a list of recommendation IDs and an idempotency_token; returns operation_id immediately for async apply
API: POST /v1/optimize/undo - accepts operation_id or recommendation IDs and is idempotent
Server: apply operations are recorded in an operation_log with at-least-once processing guarded by dedup using idempotency_token and sequence checks
SDK: helpers for createApply(), waitForCompletion(operation_id), and safeRetry(createApply) that encapsulate backoff and token reuse

Webhooks: operation lifecycle events (started, progress, completed, failed, rolled_back) posted to customer-configured endpoints with HMAC signature and retry semantics; failures land in DLQ with admin alerts
Integration tests: simulate controller restart and duplicate retries and demonstrate no-double-application and successful rollbacks
Console: operation visible in Optimize > Activity with per-step logs and per-token cost delta snapshot
Audit: every state change emits an audit log entry with user/actor, timestamp, operation_id, and before/after config snapshot
tasks: Spec: document API contract and webhook payloads in Confluence (link below)
Implementation: server endpoints, operation_log schema, and transaction coordinator
SDK: Node+Python client helpers to manage idempotency tokens and polling
Test: unit tests for dedup, integration tests for controller restarts and parallel retries
Security: request signing for webhooks and RBAC checks for undo operations
Observability: tracing spans, per-operation metrics, and DLQ dashboard
notes:
Design choices considered: using optimistic concurrency with sequence numbers vs. a single-leader apply coordinator; chosen approach is leaderless guarded by a strongly-unique idempotency_token combined with lightweight compare-and-swap on the operation_log to avoid needing a global lock. We will store minimal before/after diffs to minimize storage and enable fast rollback.

Trade-offs: leader approach would simplify ordering but introduces single-point-of-failure / takeover complexity for Dedicated/Private where customers may manage control planes. A token+CAS approach is more portable.

Data model sketch (kept short here): operation_log(entry_id, operation_id, idempotency_token, actor, state, items_applied[], prev_snapshot_hash, created_at, updated_at). Items_applied is stored as a serializable list; prev_snapshot_hash references a snapshot store for diffs.

Webhook payload sample and HMAC header are documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/optimize/apply-api#webhook-contract
API spec (OpenAPI draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/blob/main/api/apply-openapi.yaml
Reference GH PR for initial server changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/1427
implementation_notes:
Server: use existing control-plane event store and extend with a small operation coordinator service. The apply handler must validate idempotency_token and atomically insert a new operation row with state=queued using a scoped DB transaction. Worker processes claim queued operations using 'claim_token' + CAS on state for guaranteed single worker execution.

Retry model: clients can re-POST same idempotency_token; server responds with existing operation_id. Workers are idempotent and check operation_log to skip reapplying items already recorded in items_applied. Rollback performs reverse-application using stored prev_snapshot by applying compensating changes and then sets state=rolled_back.

Observability: attach trace_id to operation and propagate to webhook events. Emit Prometheus metrics: optimize_apply_requests_total, optimize_apply_retries, optimize_apply_rollback_total, optimize_apply_duration_seconds_bucket.

SDK: expose an ApplyContext object that generates/reuses idempotency tokens (UUIDv4 or customer-specified), attaches metadata (actor, source), and exposes safeRetry(fn) which will reuse the token across retry attempts. Provide examples for serverless controllers that may lose in-memory tokens and need to persist them in Redis or DB.
risks: Partial apply if worker crashes between applying some items and persisting items_applied - mitigated by batching atomic DB updates and durable commit ordering
Increased operation_log growth - mitigation: TTL for fully-completed operations and compressed diffs for snapshots
Webhook delivery at scale - mitigation: per-customer rate limits and DLQ backed by SQS/Kafka with retention settings
Compatibility: Private deployments with air-gapped control planes may need different DLQ/backplane configs
